newsitem.title: USA: Anheuser Busch boosting stake in Mexican brewer.
newsitem.headline: Anheuser Busch boosting stake in Mexican brewer.

text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc. said Friday it will again raise its stake in the brewer of Corona beer, Mexico's Grupo Modelo SA de CV, investing $550 million to boost its holding to 50.2 percent.
Anheuser-Busch, the world's largest brewer, said it expects to complete the purchase, which will bring its total investment in Grupo Modelo to about $1.6 billion, sometime later this year.
Anheuser-Busch in May raised its stake in Grupo Modelo and its subsidiaries to 37 percent for $605 million.

The St. Louis-based brewing giant acquired a 17.7 percent interest in Grupo Modelo and its Diblo SA de CV subsidiary in 1993. It had options to increase its investments to 50.2 percent by the end of 1997.
The company said last month that its board authorised its remaining options to be exercised before the end of the year. The timing and price, however, had not yet determined.
"Given Anheuser's strategy of increasing its penetration of the international beer business, this comes as no surprise," Oppenheimer analyst Roy Burry said of the latest purchase.

Anheuser-Busch, maker of Budweiser, Busch and Michelob beers, holds a 45 percent share of the U.S. beer market. It has been expanding its international business, largely through ventures and investments in other brewers. For example, it also has an alliance with Kirin Brewery Co. Ltd. of Japan.
"Our investment in Modelo is a key element in our strategy for international growth," Chairman August Busch III said in a statement.
"Mexico is the seventh-largest beer market in the world. With highly favourable demographics and relatively low per-capita consumption, there is signficant growth potential in this market."
Modelo's brands include Corona, Modelo Especial, Pacifico, Negra Modelo and a number of regional brands brewed at eight breweries in Mexico.
